Research:Open CC BY V4.0 ubir@bolton.ac.uk Innovation in Aging, 2024, 8, 1–10 https://doi.org/10.1093/geroni/igad140 Advance access publication 2 January 2024 Special Issue: Aging in Sub-Saharan Africa: Original Research Article Aging and Caring: Exploring Older Adults’ Motivation for Informal Caregiving to Other Aging Individuals in Nigeria Juliet Chigozie Donatus Ezulike, PhD1,2,*, , Shiyu Lu, PhD,3, and Marcus Yu Lung Chiu, PhD4,5, 1Department of Social and Behavioural Sciences, City University of Hong Kong, Kowloon, Hong Kong, People’s Republic of China. In Nigeria, the African coun-try with the largest population of adults aged 60 years and older, self-construal rooted in the African collectivist philosophy generally shapes informal caregiving for older adults. This study explored older adults’ motives for informal caregiving to their care recipients in urban Southeast Nigeria.
